name: Stair Climber
summary: A continuous cyclical climbing exercise performed on a revolving staircase or stepping machine to build lower-body endurance and aerobic capacity.

setup: Step onto the pedals or lower steps of the stair climber machine.
Select your program or set the stepping speed to a manageable pace before pressing start.
Stand tall with chest lifted, shoulders back, and place your hands lightly on the handrails for balance only.
steps: Step fully onto each rising step with your entire foot, avoiding hanging your heels off the edge.
Push through the midfoot and heel of the lead leg to elevate your body smoothly.
Alternate legs in a continuous, controlled rhythm, keeping your hips square and torso upright.
Maintain a steady cadence without bouncing, skipping steps, or leaning forward excessively.
instructions.breathing: Breathe rhythmically in through your nose and out through your mouth, matching your breath to your stepping cadence.

common_faults.fault: Leaning heavily onto the handrails with arms supporting upper body weight.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the machine speed and use the rails only for light balance, supporting all of your body weight on your legs.

common_faults.fault: Stepping only on the balls of the feet with heels hanging off the steps.
common_faults.correction: Place the entire foot flat on each step to maximize glute and quad recruitment and protect the Achilles tendon.
Keep your chest up and spine neutral with a slight natural forward lean from the ankles.

precautions: Familiarize yourself with the machine's emergency stop button before beginning.
Start at a low stepping rate to ensure steady rhythm before increasing speed.
